subject: ClearHealth: Compliance evidence pack + KMS/retention exception path
messages:
From: Anna Wong <anna.wong@clearhealth.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 09 Jan 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Compliance evidence pack + KMS/retention question

Hi Sean,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team was impressed with the latency and routing controls. As we start our procurement process, Security needs a short compliance evidence pack and clarification on one technical exception path. Specifically: 

- Can you share your latest SOC2 report and a manifest of what audit logs (authn, admin actions, model requests) are retained and for how long?
- We have a requirement to keep PHI traces in our environment under our keys for a subset of workloads. Does Redwood support a BYOK/KMS exception for private deployments or a customer-managed HSM integration? If not, what is the formal exception process (artifacts, approvals, SLO changes)?

We want to get this to our InfoSec and Procurement teams early. If you can send a short pack and proposed next steps by Monday that would be ideal.

Thanks,
Anna Wong
Infosec Lead, ClearHealth

---

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Wong <anna.wong@clearhealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 09 Jan 2026 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Compliance evidence pack + KMS/retention question

Hi Anna — great to hear from you and glad the demo was useful. I'm attaching the SOC2 (redacted where necessary) and a lightweight manifest that shows which log classes we capture today (auth, admin, request/response metadata). See attachment names: SOC2_report_v3.pdf, evidence_manifest.csv.

Quick answers up front:
- Hosted API: standard retention + per-tenant metadata logs (30 days by default, configurable up to 90 days on paid tiers).
- Private (VPC/on-prem): customer-managed control plane with KMS integration is supported for Dedicated & Private customers; we can do BYOK for disk and key wrapping, but there are operational caveats for per-request model KV caching and ephemeral state (we can explain).
- Formal exception path: Security review + signed exception form + tech runbook + timeframe. I'll loop Security and Product to propose a concrete path for your PHI use case.

Neha / Grace — can you weigh in on what artifacts we need from ClearHealth to evaluate a BYOK exception and what retention knobs are on the roadmap?

Next steps: I'll set a short triage call early Monday to align stakeholders and outline required artifacts.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

---

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Anna Wong <anna.wong@clearhealth.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 08:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Compliance evidence pack + KMS/retention question

Anna / Sean — thanks for raising this. For a BYOK exception with PHI, Security needs the following artifacts before we can sign off on any exception: 

1) Data flow diagram for the workloads that will use customer keys (where tokens, KV cache, and temporary model context are stored).
2) Proposed key lifecycle: key rotation schedule, KMS provider (AWS KMS / Azure KeyVault / HSM vendor), and access control list for key operators.
3) Expected retention windows for request/response pairs and for any persisted audit logs.
4) A runbook describing emergency key revoke and data deletion procedures.
5) Contractual language requirements (we can share a template exception addendum).

On log retention: we currently capture three classes: 1) Control-plane admin logs (retained 1y), 2) Auth/identity events (90d default, can extend), 3) Inference request metadata (30d default in hosted; in Private deployments customers can specify retention in the config). We do not persist full user prompt content in hosted by default unless enabled — that's an important distinction.

I suggest we treat this as a scoped exception for ClearHealth's dedicated private deployment. Sean — can you confirm the target topology (VPC private control plane vs fully on-prem)? If it's fully on-prem we have a different checklist.

Neha Kapoor
Head of Security, Redwood Inference

---

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Anna Wong <anna.wong@clearhealth.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Compliance evidence pack + KMS/retention question

Hi all — product / infra perspective: 

- Roadmap: we have a Q2 plan to expose per-tenant retention controls for inference metadata and audit logs in Private and Dedicated modes (admin toggle + retention days). That will let compliance teams pin retention to their SLOs.
- BYOK: for Private deployments we already support customer-managed KMS for disk encryption and key wrapping of persisted stores (S3, attached volumes). We do not currently support per-request encryption of KV cache in the runtime; that is complicated due to performance concerns. We can propose a mitigations list: strict TTLs on KV cache, encrypted swap, and ephemeral in-memory only for PHI workloads.
- Exception path: if customer needs a guarantee we can do a short-term exception (3–6 months) with additional operational controls + weekly audit reports. We will need engineering time to implement the logging hooks required for your auditors — estimate ~2 sprints for the minimal evidence pack endpoints.

Action items:
1) Sean: confirm ClearHealth topology and procurement timeline.
2) Anna: send the data-flow diagram and proposed retention windows.
3) Grace / Dylan: we'll prepare a scope doc and resource estimate for the two-sprint effort.

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Product Manager, Platform

---

From: Anna Wong <anna.wong@clearhealth.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 16:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Compliance evidence pack + KMS/retention question

Thanks — that all looks good. We're targeting a production pilot in March (timeline driven by a vendor evaluation window). I'll attach the data-flow diagram by EOD tomorrow and set a procurement cadence note with our legal team. For the exception, ClearHealth's preference is a VPC private control plane with customer-managed keys (AWS KMS). Please include the exception addendum template and the weekly audit report cadence in the scope doc.

Anna Wong
Infosec Lead, ClearHealth

Attachments referenced: SOC2_report_v3.pdf (SOC2 summary), evidence_manifest.csv (log classes + current retention), requested_controls_checklist.xlsx (initial control questions)
